tour.title: Project Scope and Rules
tour.description: Start with the README and knowledge-base index to understand the personal project/task application and its local and Telegram-account modes. The architecture guide maps the modules used in the following steps, while AGENTS.md records preservation rules and verification boundaries. These references distinguish implemented behavior from historical checks and remaining limitations.

tour.title: Browser Entry and Composition
tour.description: The browser entry mounts React, loads shared styles and registers the public offline shell. App.jsx then connects workspace state to navigation, task/project views and dialogs. Read this broad composition point before following its dependencies into domain state and persistence.

tour.title: Workspace Rules and State
tour.description: The model defines compatible snapshots, ordering, filtering and derived task groups used throughout the interface. Pure workspace mutations and dashboard selectors keep updates separate from rendering, while useWorkspace coordinates guarded saves, optimistic feedback and retained form drafts. This boundary explains how views can offer immediate actions without treating a preview as confirmed persistence.

tour.title: Shared Content and Language
tour.description: The workspace descriptions and interface labels rely on shared content rules. English/Russian messages and language subscriptions support both browser and bot surfaces, while Markdown rendering suppresses unsafe links and automatic external image requests. Legacy description normalization preserves old checklist content without requiring users to resave it.

tour.title: Views and Mobile Interaction
tour.description: Dashboard and Kanban components present the derived task collections from the workspace layer. The drag hook handles mouse, touch Move controls and keyboard movement, while shell and responsive styles define scrolling panes and mobile layouts. These implementation boundaries are relevant to mobile rendering reports, but do not by themselves prove the intermittent physical-iPhone artifact is resolved.

tour.title: Durable Browser Synchronization
tour.description: The repository selector switches between local browser storage and the authenticated remote repository. Server-mode edits use account-scoped IndexedDB state and queues, and the merge layer combines nonoverlapping fields while exposing conflicting changes. The request wrapper bounds HTTP work so the state layer can preserve queued edits and report failures instead of silently discarding them.

tour.title: Authenticated Server Storage
tour.description: The remote repository connects to the Node application introduced here. Browser-bound Telegram authentication supplies ownership for snapshot, settings and attachment APIs, while SQLite transactions enforce revision/idempotency checks and account isolation. Server validation and the API documentation define the accepted data contract before client changes become durable account state.

tour.title: Attachment Content and Metadata
tour.description: Shared attachment helpers validate metadata and file content and construct portable backups. Authenticated APIs store private account-owned content in SQLite, while browser IndexedDB retains local content separately from workspace metadata. The remote repository uploads required files before snapshot operations, connecting the durable queue from the previous steps to attachment-preserving saves.

tour.title: Additive Import and Backups
tour.description: The import form previews a validated template or portable backup before adding data to the current workspace. The parser and append logic create new IDs, merge Inbox tasks and retain existing projects, using the attachment helpers when backup content includes files. The public template and import guide make this contract reviewable without exposing personal workspace data.

tour.title: Telegram Capture and Reminders
tour.description: Telegram uses the same account storage and shared language messages rather than a separate task model. The bot handles confirmation-based sign-in, Inbox capture, task-form links and durable daily delivery. Daily summaries and /today include unfinished Inbox tasks independently of due dates, so unallocated work is visible alongside the existing today-task reminder.

tour.title: Build and Offline Shell
tour.description: Webpack and its service-worker plugin package the interface already explored in the tour. The browser registration module enables the public application shell to reopen offline, while private task data and pending edits belong to repository storage. Package scripts tie these build steps to development and release preparation.

tour.title: Synthetic Verification Boundaries
tour.description: The test setup runs separate development, preview and simulated backend servers with synthetic accounts and tasks. Attachment unit/browser tests exercise content preservation and download flows, while feedback tests cover pending responses, rejection and draft retention. These checks support the implementation contracts without establishing deployment status or reproducing every physical-device rendering symptom.

tour.title: Exact Releases and Recovery
tour.description: Release tooling packages a clean exact commit and verifies archive checksums and revision identity before explicit upload or installation. The deployment script backs up SQLite and restores the previous code if startup or health checks fail; systemd and Nginx examples define the production process and proxy boundaries. Follow the VPS guide for applying these operations, because local implementation and successful checks do not establish a running production release.
